search_surface: Targeted PyPI project pages and project documentation for the first nine leads; then the PyPI Simple JSON project-name index filtered locally (seven name queries, first 100 alphabetical hits each) with a top-15,000 PyPI package list used only to pick plausible high-adoption leads; see registry-snapshot.json

adoption_metric.name: PyPI Stats last_month downloads excluding known mirrors
adoption_metric.observation_window: rolling last month on observation date
adoption_metric.limitation: Downloads measure package adoption, not XML-specific use. Some packages are generic HTML/XML wrappers or transitive dependencies. Leads are not a verified parser ranking.

leads.name: et-xmlfile
leads.reason: Incremental XML writer (an implementation of lxml.xmlfile for openpyxl); it has no API that parses XML input. Serializer, not a parser path.

leads.name: beautifulsoup4
leads.family_hint: lxml/libxml2 XML backend (shared with lxml; no independent XML tokenizer)

leads.name: defusedxml
leads.family_hint: guarded CPython xml.etree.ElementTree XMLParser / pyexpat / Expat (shared with xmltodict, untangle and ElementTree)

leads.name: elementpath
leads.reason: XPath 1.0-3.1 and XSD datatype processor over caller-supplied ElementTree or lxml trees; it does not read XML bytes. Not a parser path.

leads.name: xmlschema
leads.api_hint: xmlschema.XMLResource(local XML byte stream); root, get_xmlns, get_namespaces
leads.family_hint: xmlschema XMLResource over CPython xml.etree.ElementTree.iterparse / pyexpat / Expat (shared with xmltodict, untangle, defusedxml and ElementTree)

leads.name: selectolax
leads.reason: HTML5 parser bindings (Lexbor/Modest); HTML tokenizers are excluded by the XML cell protocol.

leads.name: scrapy
leads.reason: scrapy.Selector is a subclass of the selected parsel.Selector; Selector(text=..., type='xml') runs the same Parsel SafeXMLParser over lxml/libxml2. Same parser path and API as the selected parsel row; not counted separately.

leads.name: parsel
leads.family_hint: Parsel Selector over lxml.etree SafeXMLParser / libxml2 (shared with lxml and beautifulsoup4; no independent XML tokenizer)

leads.name: xsdata
leads.reason: Typed dataclass binding: XmlParser.from_bytes needs a target class generated from a schema. Its generic AnyElement is a wildcard field type, not a usable root view: XmlParser().from_bytes(control, AnyElement) raises 'Unknown property AnyElement:{urn:parsarium:item}item', and with fail_on_unknown_properties=False the root comes back with no name and no children (checked with xsdata 26.10 on the catalog control). Mapping layer requiring a caller schema (laravie precedent); not counted.

leads.name: pydantic-xml
leads.reason: pydantic model binding: parsing requires caller-defined BaseXmlModel classes; no generic element view. Mapping layer requiring a caller schema; not counted.

leads.name: saxonche
leads.reason: SaxonC-HE 13 XSLT/XQuery/XPath processor shipped as a GraalVM native-image library; PySaxonProcessor.parse_xml works on bytes, but the parser is closed AOT-compiled code with no source to instrument, so it cannot meet the parser-source coverage and AFL++ runnability gate. Not counted.

leads.name: tree-sitter-xml
leads.reason: tree-sitter grammar for XML and DTD: produces a concrete syntax tree of raw tokens without reference decoding or namespace processing (grammar packages are excluded by the XML cell protocol).

leads.name: pyquery
leads.family_hint: pyquery PyQuery over lxml.etree.fromstring / libxml2 (shared with lxml, beautifulsoup4 and parsel; no independent XML tokenizer)

leads.name: cmeel-tinyxml2
leads.reason: cmeel distribution of the TinyXML-2 C++ library (headers, shared library and CMake files for C++ builds); it exposes no Python parsing API.

leads.name: xmljson
leads.reason: Converts caller-supplied ElementTree/lxml Element objects to dicts with several conventions; the caller parses the bytes with lxml or ElementTree. No local-bytes parse API of its own.

leads.name: alibabacloud-tea-xml
leads.reason: Alibaba Cloud SDK helper: Client.parse_xml(body, response) runs ElementTree.fromstring and converts the tree to a dict. The README documents installation only; the method's only description is a docstring saying it parses the body into a target response model (a caller model, ignored by the 0.0.3 code). No documented generic parse API; downloads are transitive SDK installs. Not counted.

leads.name: xmltojson
leads.reason: Command-line wrapper: parse() calls the selected xmltodict.parse and json.dumps; no parsing code of its own. Same parser path as xmltodict; not counted.

leads.name: djangorestframework-xml
leads.reason: Django REST framework request parser for an ad-hoc XML payload format: XMLParser.parse drops the root name and every attribute, collapses same-name siblings (the catalog control's two item elements overwrite each other) and coerces text to int/Decimal/datetime. Fails the shared control result; not counted.

leads.name: xmldiff
leads.reason: Computes edit scripts between two lxml trees; a diff tool over lxml, not a parser path.

leads.name: untangle
leads.family_hint: defusedxml DefusedExpatParser / CPython xml.sax / Expat (shared with xmltodict and ElementTree)

leads.name: pandas-read-xml
leads.reason: Reads XML into pandas DataFrames through xmltodict (a declared dependency); no parser of its own. Not counted.

leads.name: pyaxmlparser
leads.reason: Parses Android binary AXML from APK files, not XML 1.0 text. Out of format scope.

leads.name: mwxml
leads.reason: Iterator over the MediaWiki XML dump schema (pages, revisions); schema-specific, not a generic XML element view.

leads.name: beautifulsoup
leads.reason: Beautiful Soup 3.2.2 (Python 2 only), the predecessor of the selected beautifulsoup4; it does not install on the cell's Python 3.14 runtime. Predecessor path; not counted.

leads.name: jxmlease
leads.family_hint: jxmlease node builder over CPython pyexpat / Expat (raw names; shared with xmltodict, untangle and ElementTree)

leads.name: xml-python
leads.reason: Builder objects map tags to caller-supplied parser and maker functions (xml_python.Builder); without that caller mapping it reports nothing. Mapping layer requiring a caller schema; not counted.

leads.name: rapidxml
leads.reason: RapidXml 2.1.4 (Python C++ extension over bundled RapidXML 1.13, the RapidXML family of the C++ cell) fails both valid controls through its documented RapidXml(bytes) API: the default flags (parse_no_data_nodes | parse_no_utf8) drop the catalog control's CDATA text 'x < y', and on the order control the decimal/hex character reference for the euro sign is stored as non-UTF-8 bytes, so reading the values raises SystemError over UnicodeDecodeError. The undocumented parse_cdata=True keyword switches to parse_declaration_node and parses both controls to the raw-name summary, but it is not part of the documented API. Not promoted in this round. Evidence: data/python/xml/rapidxml-lead-check.json.
leads.round_4_recheck: 2026-11-18: the 2.1.4 sdist was re-read. README.md documents only RapidXml(bytes) and RapidXml(path, from_file=True); no docstring or document mentions parse_cdata, which appears only as a keyword of RapidXml.__init__ in rapidxml/rapidxml.py and in the C extension's kwlist (document_object.cpp). It stays excluded.

leads.name: pygixml
leads.reason: Cython bindings over pugixml and yxml, but the published license adds a usage condition to the MIT text ('To use this software, you must star the project on GitHub'), so it is not an open-source license as written; it also ships no aarch64 Linux wheel. Not counted.

leads.name: genshi
leads.family_hint: Genshi stream builder over CPython pyexpat / Expat in namespace mode (shared with xmltodict, untangle, jxmlease and ElementTree)

leads.name: suds-community
leads.reason: Round 4: SOAP client (suds-community 1.2.0). Its suds.sax.parser.Parser builds suds' own Element tree from xml.sax events, but it is an internal module: the PyPI description and project documentation document only the WSDL Client API, not a local XML parse API. Not built.

leads.name: twisted
leads.reason: Round 4: twisted.words.xish.domish.elementStream() is an XMPP stream element builder over pyexpat: it reports the stream root as a start event and delivers each top-level child as a separate element event instead of one document tree. A protocol library's stream framing, not a general XML parser API (the C cell's libstrophe precedent). Not built.

leads.name: xmltodict-rs
leads.reason: Round 4: Rust/PyO3 xmltodict-compatible converter (0.13.10, quick-xml family, its own engine). Its 16,768 last-month downloads rank below jxmlease (118,785), the tenth path, so with the cell at its ten-path ceiling it was not built.
